details:
Q1: The bounded `ci.yml` gate is already in both release jobs. What should this issue change?
Choices:
A) Keep `release_ci_gate.sh` as it is. Replace the legacy combined-status checks in both `validate` jobs (`commits/<sha>/status`) with the same bounded `ci.yml`-run check, and keep it warning-only when `gate_only` is set. Add contract tests and a changelog fragment. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Treat the CI-gate part as already done (#6797). Only add the `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` guard (see Q2), with tests.
C) Write a new gate that replaces `release_ci_gate.sh`, exactly as the issue text says, even though it duplicates existing behaviour.
Q2: How should `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` behave, given that defaulting it off pauses all stable releases?
Choices:
A) Default `true`, used as a kill switch: setting it to `false` skips the tag writes in both release jobs with a `::warning::`. Releases keep running and the fail-closed CI gate keeps protecting them. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Default off, as the issue says: both release jobs skip every tag write until a person sets the repo variable `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED=true`. Auto-release and promote-cycle runs will not publish `stable` until then.
   **Note:** with Q1:B this pauses releases while adding no new protection, because the CI gate already exists.
C) Drop the flag. The existing fail-closed gate already makes tagging safe.
